page: Microsoft Azure D16as_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the DASv5 instance series. It is configured with 16 vCPUs and 64.0 GB of memory running on Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization. Powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC 7763 processor operating at 3.525 GHz across 8 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading, it maintains a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Cache hierarchy includes 32 KB L1 data cache, 0.5 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache per socket structure. It does not include dedicated graphics processing units or integrated local temporary storage.

Benchmark outcomes demonstrate solid performance across standard compute tasks, anchored by strong single-core compute performance in stress-ng tests (2702.48, placing in the top 25%). Multi-core results, including a stress-ng score of 21622.11 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 9957.0, fall into the median range across comparable tiers. Instruction extension benchmarks show balanced throughput across AES and SHA cryptographic instructions, Clang software builds (13935.0), and database operations (7053.52). While small-block cached read memory bandwidth operates at 1037.17 GB/sec, uncached write memory bandwidth reaches 22.9 GB/sec, positioning write throughput in the lower quartile.

The absence of integrated local NVMe storage requires reliance on remote persistent block storage options, introducing considerations for I/O path latency. In exchange, the standard memory footprint paired with dedicated AMD EPYC CPU threads delivers consistent compute capability. This hardware design fits general-purpose server operations, enterprise web serving, backend services, CI/CD application build pipelines, and moderate database or caching tiers.
description: Microsoft Azure D16as_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 x86_64 processor clocked at 3.525 GHz. It provides 16 vCPUs across 8 physical cores, accompanied by 64.0 GB of memory adhering to a balanced 1:4 CPU-to-RAM ratio. The server lacks an integrated GPU and comes without local ephemeral storage, utilizing remote disks instead. System benchmarks display top-quartile single-core performance in stress-ng and strong inference generation on lightweight language models, while multi-core workloads and Geekbench tests show steady median results. Cryptographic acceleration and robust compression performance support reliable backend tasks. Its balanced memory allocation and core configuration make it appropriate for web serving, microservice layers, software compilation, and enterprise relational database deployments relying on networked storage.
